arxiv-1407-1713.title: Membrane-protein interactions hold the key to understanding amyloid formation
arxiv-1407-1713.creator: John E. Straub 1 and D. Thirumalai 2
arxiv-1407-1713.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by John E. Straub 1 and D. Thirumalai 2. Spurred by the appreciation that protein aggregation, leading to amyloid fibril formation, is linked to a growing list of diseases there has been intense effort to understand the factors that trigger association between peptides. This vastly complex field has attracted a variety of approaches ranging from mutational studies at the genetic level to characterization of events at the molecular level of specific proteins.

arxiv-2110-10083.title: Contrastive Active Inference
arxiv-2110-10083.creator: Pietro Mazzaglia, Tim Verbelen, Bart Dhoedt
arxiv-2110-10083.description: Abstract Active inference is a unifying theory for perception and action resting upon the idea that the brain maintains an internal model of the world by minimizing free energy. From a behavioral perspective, active inference agents can be seen as self-evidencing beings that act to fulfill their optimistic predictions, namely preferred outcomes or goals.

arxiv-2211-15183.title: Continuous Episodic Control
arxiv-2211-15183.creator: Zhao Yang, Thomas. M. Moerland, Mike Preuss, Aske Plaat
arxiv-2211-15183.description: Abstract Non-parametric episodic memory can be used to quickly latch onto high-rewarded experience in reinforcement learning tasks. In contrast to parametric deep reinforcement learning approaches in which reward signals need to be back-propagated slowly, these methods only need to discover the solution once, and may then repeatedly solve the task.

arxiv-2401-11919.title: Thermodynamic work of partial resetting
arxiv-2401-11919.creator: Kristian Stølevik Olsen, Deepak Gupta
arxiv-2401-11919.description: Abstract Partial resetting, whereby a state variable x ⁡ ( t ) x(t) is reset at random times to a value a ​ x ​ ( t ) ax(t) , 0 ≤ a ≤ 1 0\leq a\leq 1 , generalizes conventional resetting by introducing the resetting strength a a as a parameter.

arxiv-2405-01064.title: A Roadmap for Simulation-Based Testing of Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems: Challenges and Future Direction Conference: International Workshop on Software Engineering in 2030; November 2024; Puerto Galinàs (Brazil)
arxiv-2405-01064.creator: Christian Birchler, Sajad Khatiri, Pooja Rani, Timo Kehrer, Sebastiano Panichella
arxiv-2405-01064.description: Abstract . As the era of autonomous cyber-physical systems (ACPSs), such as unmanned aerial vehicles and self-driving cars, unfolds, the demand for robust testing methodologies is key to realizing the adoption of such systems in real-world scenarios. However, traditional software testing paradigms face unprecedented challenges in ensuring the safety and reliability of these systems.

arxiv-2601-09444.title: Data scaling for navigation in unknown environments
arxiv-2601-09444.creator: Lauri Suomela, Naoki Takahata, Sasanka Kuruppu Arachchige, Harry Edelman, Joni-Kristian Kämäräinen
arxiv-2601-09444.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Lauri Suomela, Naoki Takahata, Sasanka Kuruppu Arachchige, Harry Edelman, Joni-Kristian Kämäräinen. Generalization of imitation-learned navigation policies to environments unseen in training remains a major challenge. We address this by conducting the first large-scale study of how data quantity and data diversity affect real-world generalization in end-to-end, map-free visual navigation.

arxiv-2602-21373.title: Fiber Link Stabilization with a Multicore Fiber Amplifier
arxiv-2602-21373.creator: Yifan Liu, Takuma Nakamura, Daniel J. Elson, Yuta Wakayama, Charles A. McLemore, Tetsuya Hayashi, Mikael Mazur, Nicolas Fontaine, Franklyn Quinlan, Nazanin Hoghooghi
arxiv-2602-21373.description: Abstract We study the use of separate cores of a multicore erbium-doped fiber amplifier (MC-EDFA) in a noise-canceled link for ultrastable optical frequency transfer. We demonstrate fractional frequency instability of 5 × 10 − 19 5\times 10^{-19} at 1000 s averaging time for the stabilized MC-EDFA alone and 1.4 × 10 − 18 1.

dio-cassius-roman-history-cary-vol-2.title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 2: Books XII-XXXV (Fragments)
dio-cassius-roman-history-cary-vol-2.creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
dio-cassius-roman-history-cary-vol-2.description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), fragments of Books 12-35, the conquest of the Mediterranean world, preserved in Byzantine excerpts, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

pmc-11391507.title: Homeostatic Regulation of Spike Rate within Bursts in Two Distinct Preparations
pmc-11391507.creator: Alishah Lakhani, Carlos Gonzalez-Islas, Zahraa Sabra, Nicholas Au Yong, Peter Wenner
pmc-11391507.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Homeostatic plasticity represents a set of mechanisms thought to stabilize some function of neural activity. Here, we identified the specific features of cellular or network activity that were maintained after the perturbation of GABAergic blockade in two different systems: mouse cortical neuronal cultures where GABA is inhibitory and motoneurons in the isolated embryonic chick spinal cord where GABA is excitatory (males and females combined in both systems). We conducted a comprehensive analysis of various spiking activity characteristics following GABAergic blockade.

pmc-11431669.title: Association of Tai Chi and Square Dance with Cognitive Function in Chinese Older Adults
pmc-11431669.creator: Xiaoguang Zhao, Dongxue Liu, Jin Wang
pmc-11431669.description: Objective: This study explores the association of Tai Chi and square dance with cognitive function and compares the effects of the two fitness programs on cognitive function in Chinese older adults. Methods: A total of 1732 older people (aged 60 years and over) met the inclusion criteria from the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey.

pmc-11677665.title: Immunoconjugates as an Efficient Platform for Drug Delivery: A Resurgence of Natural Products in Targeted Antitumor Therapy
pmc-11677665.creator: Rositsa Mihaylova, Denitsa Momekova, Viktoria Elincheva, Georgi Momekov
pmc-11677665.description: The present review provides a detailed and comprehensive discussion on antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) as an evolving new modality in the current therapeutic landscape of malignant diseases. The principle concepts of targeted delivery of highly toxic agents forsaken as stand-alone drugs are examined in detail, along with the biochemical and technological tools for their successful implementation.

pmc-12404961.title: Protective immune response in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) against the parasitic nematode Anisakis simplex
pmc-12404961.creator: Kaan Kumas, Maja Hauptmann Andersen, Rzgar Jaafar, Cyril Henard, Per Walter Kania, Kurt Buchmann
pmc-12404961.description: IntroductionParasitic nematodes are prevalent in fish populations. The parasites are pathogenic but depress host responses, which limit clearance of the pathogens from the invasion sites. We hypothesized that one of several control strategies, which could augment protection, is immunization of the fish host with parasite antigens prior to live pathogen exposure.

pmc-12747086.title: Traumatic Bronchus Avulsion Managed With Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation, Pneumonectomy, and Rib Fixation
pmc-12747086.creator: Gillian D. Hertslet, Kaylan N. Gee, Thomas W. Mazonas, Sean A. Jordan, John E. Griepentrog
pmc-12747086.description: The mortality of injuries sustained from blunt thoracic trauma (TT) is significantly higher than the mortality of penetrating injuries, and decisions made during the first hour of hospitalization play a critical role in determining outcomes. Patient survival depends on the effective management of injuries that result in the disruption of respiration, circulation, or both.

pmc-13173727.title: Isolated splenic metastasis from colorectal cancer: clinical characteristics and management
pmc-13173727.creator: Yujie Li, Jingna Hu
pmc-13173727.description: BackgroundIsolated splenic metastases from colorectal cancer (CRC) are an extremely rare clinical entity with unclear clinical characteristics. The purpose of this study was to clarify the prognostic factors, therapeutic outcomes, diagnostic methods, and clinical patterns related to this uncommon metastatic entity.MethodsWe describe a novel instance of metachronous isolated splenic metastasis treated at our institution.

pmc-13238323.title: Investigation of Contrast Retention in PCOM Aneurysms as a Possible Marker for Instability and Rupture
pmc-13238323.creator: Laurel M. M. Marsh, Fernando Mut, Alireza Chitsaz, Rainald Lohner, Anne M. Robertson, Naoki Kaneko, Juan R. Cebral
pmc-13238323.description: Identification of cerebral aneurysms at risk of destabilization and rupture remains challenging. Although flow stagnation has been recognized as a risk factor, the underlying mechanisms and its predictive power are poorly understood. The purpose was to investigate possible associations between flow stagnation determined from computational fluid dynamics (CFD)‐based virtual angiograms and aneurysm instability and rupture.
